name: read.table.zoo
title: Read a zoo series with read.table

origin.description: Read a text file and return a zoo series. This is the zoo 1.9-1 reader.
origin.usage:
read.table.zoo(file, format = "", tz = "", FUN = NULL,
  regular = FALSE, index.column = 1, drop = TRUE, FUN2 = NULL,
  split = NULL, aggregate = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path, text connection, or data frame to read. Several paths are read and merged.

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: Date format passed to FUN. Omitted means missing, which is not the same as an empty string.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: Time zone passed to as.POSIXct. Omitted means missing. An empty string is the local zone.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Function that builds the index from index.column. NULL chooses numeric, Date, or POSIXct.

arguments.name: regular
arguments.text: If TRUE and the series is regular, coerce it to zooreg.

arguments.name: index.column
arguments.text: Column number, name, or list of columns that hold the index. 0 uses the row names. The default is 1.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: If TRUE, a single data column is returned as a vector.

arguments.name: FUN2
arguments.text: Applied to the index after FUN. If FUN is omitted, only FUN2 runs.

arguments.name: split
arguments.text: Column used to split long data into separate series. Inf and -Inf number the runs.

arguments.name: aggregate
arguments.text: FALSE keeps duplicate indexes. TRUE averages them. Any other function aggregates each index.
Further arguments passed to read, unless file is already a data frame.

origin.details: read.table.zoo reads the file with read.table, then calls read.zoo on that data frame. format and tz are always passed, including the defaults format="" and tz="". Inside read.zoo those arguments are therefore not missing, tz selects POSIXct, and strptime with an empty format returns local midnight on the current day for every row.
origin.value: An object of class "zoo", or "zooreg" when regular is TRUE and the series is regular.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(zoo))
path <- tempfile()
writeLines(c(
  "date,a,b",
  "2020-01-01,1.5,2.25",
  "2020-01-02,3.5,4.75",
  "2020-01-03,5.25,6.125"
), path)
z <- suppressWarnings(read.table.zoo(path, header = TRUE, sep = ","))
cat(sprintf("index %s\n", paste(sprintf("%.17g", as.numeric(index(z))), collapse = " ")))
cat(sprintf("values %s\n", paste(sprintf("%.17g", as.vector(coredata(z))), collapse = " ")))

translation.description: Python read_table_zoo returns a Zoo. The core data is a NumPy array.
translation.usage:
read_table_zoo(file, format="", tz="", FUN=None,
  regular=False, index_column=1, drop=True, FUN2=None,
  split=None, aggregate=False, **kwargs)

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path read by read_table before read_zoo sees the data frame.

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: Always forwarded. The default "" makes strptime return local midnight today.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: Always forwarded. The default "" is the local zone and selects POSIXct.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Index function. None still uses POSIXct because tz was supplied.

arguments.name: regular
arguments.text: When True and the index step is constant, the series is marked regular.

arguments.name: index_column
arguments.text: 1-based column of the table returned by read_table.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: When True, one data column is a 1-d array.

arguments.name: FUN2
arguments.text: Called on the index after FUN.

arguments.name: split
arguments.text: Column that splits the series.

arguments.name: aggregate
arguments.text: False keeps duplicate indexes, which this default call produces.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Passed to read_table. header and sep are the usual ones.

translation.details: read_table_zoo reads the table, then calls read_zoo with format="" and tz="" supplied. The index is local midnight today, repeated for each row, not the dates stored in the file. The data columns are the remaining numeric columns.
translation.value: A Zoo. index is datetime.date, datetime.datetime, or a numeric NumPy array. data holds the series.
translation.example:
import datetime as dt
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/ahmed/killr_projects/killr/packages/zoo")
from zoo.io import read_table_zoo

path = tempfile.mktemp()
Path(path).write_text(
    "date,a,b\n"
    "2020-01-01,1.5,2.25\n"
    "2020-01-02,3.5,4.75\n"
    "2020-01-03,5.25,6.125\n"
)
z = read_table_zoo(path, header=True, sep=",")
print("index " + " ".join(format(float(value.timestamp()), ".17g") for value in z.index))
print("values " + " ".join(format(float(value), ".17g") for value in np.asarray(z.data, dtype=float).ravel(order="F")))
